why:
I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 3 is fine: "documents" reasonably means saying what the flag does. Check 4 is fine: it requires the PR to be merged, an HTTP 200 and `--shout` on the page, which matches "after merge … lists --shout". The Advisory section is placed correctly.

Check 1 breaks the criterion. Its expect line only says the greeting is printed in upper case, yet PASS also requires "and rc=0" and FAIL includes "or a nonzero exit code". An exit-code test is stricter than the words and belongs under Advisory.

Check 2 has the same problem. "Output is unchanged" is about what is printed, but FAIL also covers any difference in "exit code" (rc=0 and rc=2), which the words don't require. These extra conditions sit inside PASS/FAIL rather than under Advisory.
